facts.statement: Most Orodus species are known only from their rounded, ridge-covered teeth which were adapted for crushing prey.
facts.quote: Most species are only known from their rounded, ridge covered teeth, designed for crushing prey (durophagy).

facts.statement: The species O. greggi grew to approximately 2 to 4 meters in length, while O. micropterygius reached about 1 meter.
facts.quote: O. greggi reached around 2-4 m long, while O. micropterygius just reached 1 m.

facts.statement: The largest species, O. ramosus, had teeth about 11 cm wide, leading to size estimates of 12 to 15 meters, though these figures are considered unreasonable by researchers.
facts.quote: The largest species, O. ramosus, had a tooth width about 11 cm, and cross-scaling those teeth with related species with known body fossils implies a total length of 12-15 m, although these estimates have been considered unreasonable.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows that Orodus species lacked dorsal fin spines, possessed small pectoral fins, and had teeth that varied in shape based on their position in the mouth.
facts.quote: These remains show that these species of Orodus lacked fin spines on their dorsal fins, and that they had small pectoral fins, and that the morphology of the teeth varied depending on their position in the mouth.

facts.statement: Orodus is thought to be most closely related to living chimaeras among orodontiforms.
facts.quote: Like other orodontiforms, the closest living relatives of Orodus are thought to be chimaeras.

facts.statement: Orodus fossils have been found in Europe, Asia, and North America dating from the late Devonian to the Late Carboniferous periods.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from the late Devonian to Late Carboniferous of Europe, Asia and North America.

facts.statement: Orodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Orodus spans from the Frasnian to the Wordian, between 382.31 and 264.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Wordian (382.31 to 264.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Orodus was originally described by Agassiz in 1838.
De Koninck is cited as the parent authority for the genus Orodus in 1878.

rejected.statement: Orodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the group orodontiforms, named for its beautiful teeth.
rejected.quote: Orodus (from Greek, 'beautiful' and 'tooth') is an extinct genus of orodontiform cartilaginous fish.
